To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ANKRD2 protein is a short‐life protein regulated by the ubiquitin–proteasome pathway.
the ANKRD2/CARP protein is a short‐living protein whose levels are regulated by the 20S and 26S proteosomes, and that this regulation is mediated by PEST motifs within the ANKDR2 protein sequence.
ANKRD 1 is a short-lived protein that is regulated by the 20S/26S proteasomal machinery and whose stability is controlled by a PEST domain and other degrons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of a new protein degradation pathway that controls the levels of a key player in the regulation of the cardiac gene expression programme.
the identification of novel regulatory mechanisms that control the ANKRD2/CARP protein levels, and the definition of the intracellular pathways involved.
the identification of the molecular mechanisms that regulate ANKRD1 intracellular levels and provides new insights into the control of this protein's steady‐level.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ANKRD 1 protein levels are tightly regulated and that the 26S‐proteasome is a critical player in the control of ANKRD1 levels.
the 26S‐mediated proteolysis is a major pathway for controlling the steady‐state levels of the ANKRD protein.
ANKRD2 and ANKRD3 are the only two ANKRD family members that do not require the 26S‐mediated proteasomal degradation for their intracellular regulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ANKRDI protein levels are regulated through a complex network of intracellular mechanisms which include a PEST motif, ubiquitination and the 26S‐proteasome‐mediation of protein degradation.
ANKRD 1 protein levels are controlled by a complex network of intracellular pathways, including the 26S‐proteasome‐mediating proteolytic machinery and the ubiquitination system.
ANKRD2, a protein that has a high degree of sequence homology with ANKRD1, is a long‐lived protein which is not targeted to the 26S‐proteasome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 26S‐mediated control of ANKRD1 levels represents an additional layer in the complex regulatory network controlling the expression of this important gene.
the regulation of the ANKRD2/CARP protein is similar to that of other transcriptional regulators, such as the myogenic factor MyoD.
the ANKRD2/CARP protein is a short‐living protein whose steady‐state levels are regulated through proteasomal degradation.
